correctness.rationale: For real FBL^(2)[ell_2^(a+b)], a>=3, b>=2, the norm of the supremum of cross-edge evaluation magnitudes and clique amplitudes is the absolutely 2-summing norm of the row operator into ell_infty. Finite-dimensional Pietsch domination and covariance minimax yield max over edge probabilities of tr sqrt(C_w). Operator concavity and averaging over S_a x S_b reduce without restriction to total clique mass u. The Laplacian eigenvalues are (1-u)/a+2t^2u/(a-1) of multiplicity a-1, (1-u)/b of multiplicity b-1, and (a+b)(1-u)/(ab) of multiplicity 1. Strictly concave objective (a-1)*sqrt(1/a+du)+K*sqrt(1-u) has u=0 optimum precisely t<=tau; for t>tau an interior exact Cauchy-Schwarz optimizer gives the claimed radical branch. A supporting hyperplane at cross-only covariance proves the simultaneous iff s_e<=tau for any collection of nonuniform clique edges: every inactive derivative <=B/2 exactly under this bound and any superthreshold edge permits a strictly profitable mass shift. Pointwise growth for s>1/2, fixed-a fourth-root imbalance, and curvature jump follow algebraically. An independent full-coordinate incidence-matrix eigensolver with an 3001-point orbit-mass grid verified 20 parameter/weight cases. These tests corroborate rather than establish general Pietsch minimax or all-weight screening.

value.rationale: An explicit operator-ideal norm for a natural graph deformation, with the nonobvious fact that arbitrarily many individually weighted internal edges can be jointly invisible and with an unbounded fourth-root threshold under part imbalance, is meaningful structural information about FBL norms. The second-derivative transition distinguishes strict regimes; result is not merely evaluation of a fixed finite matrix.

limitations: Real exponent 2 over finite Euclidean generator space only; nonuniform amplitude iff applies on complete-bipartite background, not arbitrary graphs.
Symmetric optimum suffices for value, but every non-symmetric optimizer is not classified.
